readme:
# NPI Registry Scraper: US Healthcare Providers

Search the US National Provider Identifier (NPI) Registry and export the matching providers as a dataset. The data comes from the official public register published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (the NPPES NPI Registry). The actor returns only what the register publishes for each record and adds nothing from other sources.

Use it to build provider lists by state, city, ZIP code or specialty, to check NPI numbers, to keep a local copy of a market segment, or to feed provider data into your own systems.

Data comes from [the NPPES NPI Registry](https://npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/).

## What you get

For every NPI record:

- NPI number and type (NPI-1 for an individual provider, NPI-2 for an organization)
- Name, credential, name prefix and suffix, and gender when the register publishes it (individuals)
- Organization name, parent organization and sub-part flag (organizations)
- Primary specialty and all specialties, each with taxonomy code, description, license number and license state
- Practice location and mailing address, each with phone and fax when published
- Additional practice locations, other names (for example Doing Business As), other identifiers and endpoints when the register lists them
- Authorized official of an organization: name, title and phone
- Enumeration date, certification date, last update date and status
- A link to the record in the NPI Registry and the time it was read

## Input

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | list | Optional list of 10-digit NPI numbers to look up, one request per number |
| `state` | text | Two-letter state code, for example `CA` |
| `city` | text | City name |
| `postalCode` | text | 5-digit ZIP code, or the first digits such as `902` |
| `taxonomyDescription` | text | Specialty text as the register prints it, for example `Dentist` |
| `enumerationType` | text | `any` (default), `NPI-1` for individuals or `NPI-2` for organizations |
| `firstName`, `lastName` | text | Name of an individual provider, a trailing `*` works as a wildcard |
| `organizationName` | text | Name of an organization, a trailing `*` works as a wildcard |
| `maxResults` | number | Maximum number of providers in total. Default 100 |

At least one search value is needed. The register does not accept a search by state alone, so a search with only a state is read in parts by postal code prefix (see Limitations).

Example: dentists in California.

```json
{
  "state": "CA",
  "taxonomyDescription": "Dentist",
  "enumerationType": "any",
  "maxResults": 40
}
```

Example: organizations in Houston, Texas.

```json
{
  "state": "TX",
  "city": "Houston",
  "enumerationType": "NPI-2",
  "maxResults": 200
}
```

Example: look up NPI numbers.

```json
{
  "number": ["1760813802", "1134040793"]
}
```

## Pricing

This actor uses pay per event pricing.

| Event | Name | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Run start, charged once with the first delivered record | `actor-start` | $0.001 |
| One provider record delivered | `provider-result` | $0.0015 |

You are charged only for records that were delivered to the dataset. A run that finds nothing is not charged. Set the maximum charge per run in the run options and the actor stops cleanly when it is reached.

**New to Apify?** Every account gets a $5 free monthly platform credit, enough for a first test run before you pay anything.

## Limitations

- The register returns at most 200 records per request and accepts skip values up to 1000, so one search reaches 1200 records. When a search reaches that limit, the actor splits it by postal code prefix (two digits first, then three, four and five) and reads the parts one after another. Records are delivered once even if a part overlaps another.
- A search with a full 5-digit ZIP code or a 9-digit ZIP code cannot be split further. If such a search holds more than 1200 records, the run says so in its final status. Add a city, a specialty or a provider type to narrow it.
- Reading a large area in parts takes many requests, because every postal code prefix is one request. Requests are sent one at a time with a pause between them, so a run that covers a whole state takes a while.
- The register matches a postal code against all addresses of a record, so a record can appear for a ZIP code that is its mailing address and not its practice location.
- Only active records that the public register returns are available. The actor does not add contact details, email addresses or any data from other sources.
- Names, addresses and phone numbers of individual providers are published by the register under federal rules. You are responsible for using them in line with the laws that apply to you.
- The register can change its response format. If every answer becomes unreadable the run stops with an error and nothing is charged.

## FAQ

**Where does the data come from?**
From the official public register of the US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the NPPES NPI Registry. The actor reads the register's public search interface.

**Can I search by specialty?**
Yes. Use `taxonomyDescription` with the text the register uses, for example `Dentist`, `Family Medicine` or `Pharmacy`. A trailing `*` works as a wildcard.

**How do I get only individual providers or only organizations?**
Set `enumerationType` to `NPI-1` (individuals) or `NPI-2` (organizations).

**How many records can I get in one run?**
Up to the `maxResults` you set. Searches that reach the register's limit of 1200 records are split by postal code prefix, so large areas are possible. See Limitations.

**What happens if a number is not in the register?**
It is skipped, counted in the final status message and not charged.

**Why is a field `null`?**
The register does not publish every field for every record. Individuals have no organization name, organizations have no gender, and many records have no fax number or certification date.

**Does the run resume after an interruption?**
Yes. Progress is saved after every batch, a resumed run does not repeat delivered records and does not charge them again.

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain or LlamaIndex.

**MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=nanodata/npi-registry-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `npi-registry-scraper` to find 20 cardiologists in Texas in the NPI Registry with their practice address. Return results as a table."
